entries.clue: Crashed motor? Argument in the near future (8)

indicators.note: a crashed motor is a wrecked one, so its letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: Someone's car has been written off and a quarrel is looming.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the crash and the row look like one story, but they are two separate pieces laid end to end.
annotation.definitionFit: TOMORROW, used loosely as an adverb, means soon or in the near future.

entries.clue: Objection raised over a brass instrument (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word turns it upside down, reading it bottom to top
in a down entry, one part sits over (above) the next

blocks.note: a but = an objection, as in 'no buts'

annotation.surface: Someone is complaining about a loud brass instrument, perhaps a neighbour's practice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'But' as a noun is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tuba is one member of the brass family, its lowest voice.

entries.clue: Timid? Startled cry after first sign of mouse (4)

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter
the cry comes after the M in the answer

blocks.note: eek! is the stock startled cry

annotation.surface: A timid person shrieks at the sight of a mouse.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue writes the cartoon scene of someone screaming at a mouse; the cry itself is the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Meek means quiet, gentle and easily cowed, i.e. timid.

entries.clue: No German will get upset about one area (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting a word tips it over so it reads bottom to top
the reversed letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: GER is the standard abbreviation for German

annotation.surface: A German's refusal leaves someone annoyed about a region.
annotation.walkthrough: The German's 'no' looks like it should be NEIN; here the two words are taken separately, and the pair is flipped before the one goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a stretch of land or part of the world.

entries.clue: Someone caring for nippers relishing a toy, possibly (4,9)

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged as something else

annotation.surface: A childminder is looking after small children who love playing with a toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' reads as young children, the childminder's charges; here it means teeth, which nip.
annotation.definitionFit: An oral hygienist cleans and cares for teeth, playfully called nippers.

entries.clue: Nurse, perhaps, needing extra energy in vocation (6)

indicators.note: the carer needs something added to make the answer
'in' places the energy inside the carer, splitting CARER to take the E

blocks.note: a nurse is one kind of carer

annotation.surface: Nursing is described as a calling that demands extra energy.
annotation.walkthrough: CARER takes E into its middle: CAR(E)ER. The surface pairs nursing and vocation so the definition feels like part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: A career is one's chosen vocation or profession.

entries.clue: New party invested in a transport system without purpose (2,6)

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it

annotation.surface: A new political party puts money into a tram network with no clear aim.
annotation.walkthrough: N and DO go into A TRAM: A TRA(NDO)M. 'Party' looks political, but it is a social do.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something at random means doing it with no plan or aim, so a plain synonym for purposeless.

entries.clue: Oddly view six clues, cryptic – you won’t find them in other papers! (10)

definitions.text: you won’t find them in other papers!

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: The setter boasts of six puzzle clues that no rival paper prints.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six' is not VI here; all three of its letters join the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Exclusives are stories one paper has that no other paper carries.

entries.clue: Store? Ropy store I rebuilt (10)

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the letters together a new way

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper says they rebuilt a shabby shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter deliberately reuses 'store': once as the definition, again inside the fodder. 'Ropy' is British for poor quality.
annotation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are stored.

entries.clue: Elizabeth will swallow variety of lager in this! (4,5)

definitions.text: Elizabeth will swallow variety of lager in this!

indicators.note: the outer name takes the other letters inside it
a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Elizabeth is about to down some kind of lager from her glass.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags that the whole clue does double duty: read plainly, it describes the vessel Elizabeth drinks her lager from.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes the vessel: lager goes into it before being swallowed.

entries.clue: A lot of fish without any variety – many a kid will get stuck into that (6,7)

definitions.text: many a kid will get stuck into that

blocks.note: a school is a large group of fish

annotation.surface: A shoal of identical fish, which children love poking at.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuck into' reads as eager tucking in; here it means getting dressed in the clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Many children put on a school uniform every morning.

entries.clue: Summary regarding EU farming policy (5)

annotation.surface: A briefing summarises European agricultural policy.
annotation.walkthrough: CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy, which funds farmers.
annotation.definitionFit: A recap is a brief summary of what went before.

entries.clue: Host party before twice-yearly awards? (2,3,7)

indicators.note: one part comes before the next

blocks.note: the British honours lists come out twice a year

annotation.surface: Someone throws a party ahead of an awards ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: The British Honours list (knighthoods, OBEs and the like) is published twice a year, at New Year and on the monarch's birthday.
annotation.definitionFit: To do the honours is to act as host, serving drinks or food to guests.

entries.clue: No French song about US city will be carefree (10)

indicators.note: the song goes around the city

annotation.surface: A French song about an American city has a relaxed air.
annotation.walkthrough: NON + CHA(LA)NT, with LA tucked into CHANT.
annotation.definitionFit: Nonchalant means calm and unconcerned, i.e. carefree.

entries.clue: British farm left in trouble, ultimately – no major transport access (6,4)

indicators.note: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the end letter of the word is used

annotation.surface: A British farm is left in difficulty because it has no main road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one farm's hard luck; each word is a separate letter or chunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A branch line is a minor railway line off the main line.

entries.clue: Monster, cornered by another goblin, retreating (4)

indicators.note: trapped inside the words that follow
going backwards, so read right to left

annotation.surface: A monster is trapped in a corner by a goblin and backs away.
annotation.walkthrough: ERGO sits across the two words, and read backwards it spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating monster of folklore.

entries.clue: Land manager redistributed most grain, keeping nothing in stock (10)

indicators.note: the letters are shared out again in a new order
the fodder keeps the O among its letters

blocks.note: nothing = O, the stock of letters keeps it

annotation.surface: A farm manager redistributed most of the grain and kept nothing in reserve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most' is not a truncation signal here; its letters are part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An agronomist is an expert in soil and crop management.

entries.clue: Support for text showing American car and its maximum capacity? (8)

blocks.note: a fill is the full amount something holds

annotation.surface: A text document described with an American car and its top capacity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Text' suggests printed words; the definition is the software feature that completes typing for you.
annotation.definitionFit: Autofill supports typing text by filling in the rest of a word or form.

entries.clue: Evoked criminal before jury, not half awful prude (8,2)

indicators.note: one part comes before the next
only half of the word is used
the letters are in an awful state, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A criminal appears before a jury of which half are dreadful prudes.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture hides three separate pieces: CON + JU + REDUP.
annotation.definitionFit: To conjure up is to evoke an image or memory.

entries.clue: Fruit-tree, source of plums, getting attention (4)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
the P gets the next piece added to it

blocks.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

annotation.surface: An orchard tree is noticed for its plums.
annotation.walkthrough: The plums seem to belong to the tree; only their first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: The fruit's name doubles as the tree's name, as with apple or plum.

entries.clue: Sarcastic US spies turned up, apprehending detectives (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reverses the letters to read bottom to top
catching, so holding the next piece inside

blocks.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

annotation.surface: Scornful American agents show up and arrest some detectives.
annotation.walkthrough: CIA turned up gives AIC, which holds CID: A(CID)IC.
annotation.definitionFit: Acidic remarks are sharp and biting, i.e. sarcastic.

entries.clue: Disco pariahs, dancing to create ways of increasing desire (12)

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: Social outcasts dance at a disco in an effort to become more attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: The disco setting makes the answer feel at home.
annotation.definitionFit: Aphrodisiacs are things that increase sexual desire.

entries.clue: Perhaps Basil and Sybil’s central feature? (4)

indicators.note: the central feature of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: Sybil's = her, the possessive for a woman

annotation.surface: A question about the two Fawlty Towers hoteliers and their main quirk.
annotation.walkthrough: Basil and Sybil Fawlty are the couple running the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, but basil here is the herb.
annotation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a herb, hence 'Perhaps'.

entries.clue: US prize? Judge resigning from prize in US (4)

indicators.note: the judge resigns, leaving the word

blocks.note: a jemmy is a crowbar used to prize doors open
surface padding; the award is American

annotation.surface: A judge steps down from an American award panel.
annotation.walkthrough: The second 'prize' is not an award but the verb meaning to lever open, which is what a jemmy does.
annotation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the main US television award.

entries.clue: Liberal put in excellent explanation for absence (5)

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

annotation.surface: A Liberal politician is given a fine excuse for not showing up.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the 1 as the letter I, giving A(LIB)I.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof that one was somewhere else at the time.

entries.clue: Norwegian city starts to tempt reclusive US composer? Not at first (9)

indicators.note: take the starts, i.e. first letters, of the words
'not at first' says the word is absent at its first position, so its opening letter goes

blocks.note: Stephen SONDHEIM without his first letter

annotation.surface: A Norwegian city tries to lure a shy American composer.
annotation.walkthrough: Sondheim was the American composer of musicals like Sweeney Todd.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Trondheim is one of Norway's largest cities, on its central coast.

entries.clue: Boy soprano’s a good bet? (6)

blocks.note: the highest voice in a church choir, sung by boys
a betting term: one wager on three selections at once

annotation.surface: Someone suggests backing a young choirboy to succeed.
annotation.walkthrough: A treble in betting is a single bet on three selections, all of which must win.
annotation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy with a soprano voice, and also a three-part bet.

entries.clue: Taxi in Peruvian city backed up to yard in a friendly way (8)

indicators.note: the taxi goes inside the city
backed up means reversed, so the city reads right to left
the Y is added to what comes before

annotation.surface: A taxi in Lima reverses up to a yard in a courteous manner.
annotation.walkthrough: AMIL holds CAB, then Y is added: AMI(CAB)L + Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Amicably means in a friendly, goodwill manner.
